title: Shared-site noise had lower effective dimension than fixed-count controls in eight selected worm maps
abstract: We tested whether chemical synaptic site groups change output noise beyond source-to-target contact counts. We used eight public C. elegans brain maps and a fixed panel of 162 neurons born before hatching. The model gave each site an independent fluctuation with equal variance and gave all its targets equal positive gains. Observed covariance effective dimensions were 54.2 to 62.8. They were 4.3 to 5.9 percent below the means of controls that kept each source-to-target count and each site target count. No control draw had dimension as low as observed in any map. Each map had two chains of 500 draws. Target variance normalization gave the same direction in all maps. These results show a structural effect under the model. They do not measure release covariance, neural activity, coding loss, or a population age effect. Site geometry and functional target identity remain uncontrolled. Code, retained site groups, covariance matrices, file hashes, sampler checks and a figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Shared-site model dimensions for eight selected maps. Gray bars are conditional swap ranges, not animal confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Reuses its verified fixed panel of 162 neurons. Its cycle test is prior context; no analysis code or numerical tables reused.
